abstract: The North American Broadcasters Association’s Technical Committee (NABA-TC) plays a key role in ensuring that the technical needs and goals of our members are addressed in the complex, rapidly changing technical environment of broadcasting and content distribution. NABA’s TC works to ensure that North American broadcasting interests are represented well in key international forums. A delegation representing NABA positions participates in Working Group meetings and World Radio communication Conferences (WRCs) of the International Telecommunication Union’s Radiocommunication Sector (ITU-R), the U.N. agency with legal authority over the world radio spectrum allocations and recommendations.

authors.bio: John Lee is the chairman of the World Broadcasting Unions’ (WBUs) Technical Committee (TC) as well as the chair of the North American Broadcasters Association (NABA)’s Cybersecurity Subcommittee. He is currently a digital engineering consultant working for several large organizations. Previously, he was an executive director, technology solutions with CBC/Radio-Canada, Montreal, QC, Canada, Canada’s national public broadcaster, where he served for 38 years. In this role, he was responsible for the provision of engineering services, including digital television and radio transmission facilities, satellite and telecommunications networks, and for IT, including mobility services, UC, applications, information security, and governance. He was a winner of the Academy of Canadian Cinema and Television’s Gemini Award for Outstanding Technical Achievement.
authors.name: John Lee

authors.bio: Morwen Williams is the director of U.K. Operations with BBC News, London, U.K., leading the technical and studio teams of BBC News. She is responsible for creative technical newsgathering as well as all news studios in London and Salford at Media City, U.K. and editing in London. Altogether, a team of more than 700 people. She is the chair of the World Broadcasting Unions (WBUs) International Media Connectivity Group (IMCG), working with other broadcasters to find common solutions in this area. She is an alumni of the Media Transformation Challenge, Harvard University’s Kennedy School, Cambridge, MA. She is a keen supporter of the BBC’s apprentice schemes to deliver new and more diverse technical talent to the BBC, as well as working with the BBC News Women in Technology program. Williams has been a mentor for RISE Women in Broadcasting and the John Schofield Trust for young journalists. She is proud to have been RISE Women in Broadcasting’s Woman of the Year in 2019.
authors.name: Morwen Williams

authors.bio: Shawn Kelly is the chair of the Technical Committee (TC) for the North American Broadcasters Association (NABA). In addition, Kelly is an executive vice president of technology with Corus Entertainment Inc., Toronto, ON, Canada, responsible for leading Corus’ overall technology strategy for broadcast engineering, operations, IT, and digital media. Kelly’s focus is on technology transformation and driving solutions that enable the success of Corus’ advertising business.
